title: Vidu AI review: free credits, Q3, pricing & alternatives
summary: Vidu AI explained: Q3, free credits, reference-to-video, native audio, API pricing, limitations and four alternatives for real workflows.
body_markdown:
**Vidu AI is a short-form video generator for text-to-video, image-to-video, start/end-frame animation, and reference-guided video. Its clearest differentiator is reference-to-video: you can reuse character, object, scene, style, camera, and effect references across shots. Vidu is free to try with signup and daily-login credits, but the public web pricing page does not expose a stable plan table without loading the app, so confirm the live credit allowance and renewal price before paying.**


Vidu is most relevant when you need recurring characters or products across several short shots, or want Vidu Q3's documented native audio and clips up to 16 seconds. It is less suitable when the job depends on a full editing timeline, long-form assembly, or a predictable budget based only on a subscription headline. This review separates Vidu's web app from its API and shows how to compare alternatives with the same input.


We checked Vidu's product pages, web pricing FAQ, API documentation, API pricing, and current Q3 documentation on September 12, 2026. We did not run a controlled visual-quality or speed benchmark. Capability claims below are attributed to current first-party documentation; use the included test protocol to evaluate output for your own brief.


- **Best for:** **short narrative, character-led clips, product shots, and multi-shot concepts that need reusable visual references**
- **Main workflows:** text-to-video, image-to-video, start/end-to-video, and reference-to-video
- **Documented models:** Q3 supports native audio and up to 16 seconds; Q4 Preview now has separate image and reference API routes
- **Reference inputs:** Vidu's web product says one to seven reference images can guide characters, objects, scenes, style, composition, camera movement, and effects
- **Free access:** signup bonus credits, daily-login credits, and event credits; the amount can change by account or promotion
- **Web billing:** subscription, purchased, and bonus credits have different expiration rules
- **API billing:** separate pay-as-you-go credits; one API credit is currently listed at $0.005
- **Main caveat:** a good single clip does not prove identity, product, or scene consistency across a finished sequence


Magic Hour publishes this guide and includes its own product in the comparison. Treat the recommendations as editorial guidance from a vendor, and verify the linked first-party product details and your own output requirements before choosing a tool.


## What is Vidu AI?


[Vidu](https://www.vidu.com/) is a generative image and video platform from ShengShu Technology. The consumer product runs in a browser and mobile app. The separate[Vidu API platform](https://platform.vidu.com/) exposes model endpoints for developers.


*Vidu official product page, captured September 25, 2026. Any sample outputs or performance statements visible here are the vendor’s examples and claims, not our independent test results.*[View official source](https://www.vidu.com/)


The product name can refer to three different things:


1. **Vidu's creator app:** the no-code interface, templates, credit plans, and account library.
2. **Vidu's Q-series models:** the video models selected inside a workflow. Current documentation includes Q4 Preview, Q3 and earlier Q2 and Q1 routes; their supported inputs and billing differ.
3. **Vidu's API:** a separately billed developer platform with text, image, start/end, and reference endpoints.


Keep those layers separate. A feature shown on the consumer site may use different settings, credits, or availability from an API endpoint. A model price in the API documentation is not the cost of a web subscription.

## Is Vidu AI free?


Vidu is free to try, but “free” means a limited credit allowance rather than unlimited production use. The current[Vidu pricing FAQ](https://www.vidu.com/pricing) says new accounts receive signup bonus credits and can earn credits through daily login, events, competitions, or the Artist Program.


Vidu describes three credit types:


- **Subscription credits** come with a plan and are valid for 30 days.
- **Purchased credits** are bought separately and are valid for two years.
- **Bonus credits** come from promotions or activities and are valid for two years.


The plan cards load dynamically and were not reliably exposed in the public page we checked. That means a fixed free-credit count or monthly plan price copied from another review may already be wrong. Open the live pricing screen in your own account and record the plan price, renewal cadence, included credits, expiration, watermark or download rules, concurrency, and commercial terms before subscribing. Vidu's FAQ also says Stripe subscriptions renew automatically and that purchases are nonrefundable.


## How much does the Vidu API cost?


Vidu’s[API pricing page](https://platform.vidu.com/docs/pricing) is separate from consumer subscription pricing. Its[live USD API pricing view](https://platform.vidu.com/pricing) was verified October 10, 2026 and displays a standard rate of **$0.005 per credit** . The page labels its converted figures as estimates and directs buyers to the Console for live pricing. Generation credits depend on model, mode, duration and resolution. Q3 Pro’s documented credit rates produce these USD base-rate examples:


- **1080p:** 24 credits per second, or $0.12 per generated second
- **720p:** 20 credits per second, or $0.10 per generated second
- **540p:** 9 credits per second, or $0.045 per generated second


The same table lists lower off-peak rates for supported routes.[Current API pricing documentation](https://platform.vidu.com/docs/overview/pricing) says Q3 Pro and Q3 Turbo support off-peak only when audio is true, and Q3 Mix has no off-peak pricing. Do not assume a silent Q3 request receives that discount. Earlier Q2 modes use starting charges plus per-second credits, so do not reuse a Q3 calculation for a Q2, reference, start/end or multi-frame request.


For example, ten eight-second Q3 Pro generations at 720p contain 80 generated seconds. At the standard $0.005-per-credit conversion and 20 credits per second, the base-rate estimate is **$8.00** before tax and separate image, audio, editing, storage or delivery costs. If only two clips pass review, generation spend per accepted clip is $4.00, not $0.80. Those are hypothetical acceptance counts, not measured Vidu results; use the actual credit debit and your purchased credit unit price for the final project budget.


Use this budget formula:


**cost per accepted clip = total generation charges ÷ clips that pass the delivery checklist**


Record failed requests and completed outputs that you reject. Vidu’s current API pricing documentation says failed generation, including moderation failure, does not deduct credits. That does not exempt a completed clip merely because it misses your brief. Keep failure and review time in the workflow record while using actual charged credits in the cost calculation.


## Vidu Q3: what the current documentation says


[Vidu Q3](https://www.vidu.com/vidu-q3) is a documented Vidu model family; it should not stand in for every newer Vidu route. Its product page says one generation can produce up to 16 seconds at a time and can create visuals with dialogue, voiceover, sound effects, and music together. The page lists English, Japanese, and Chinese output, multi-speaker conversations, and camera and pacing controls.


Those are provider claims, not independent measurements. Before choosing Q3 for production, test whether the requested words are spoken correctly, the intended speaker owns each line, sound effects arrive at the right moment, music does not bury speech, and the final container works in your editing stack.


Longer clips can reduce stitching, but duration alone does not guarantee narrative continuity. A 16-second result can still drift in wardrobe, product shape, background, lighting, or shot logic. Evaluate every required beat rather than treating maximum duration as usable duration.


### Q4 Preview: check the endpoint before migrating


Vidu now documents separate[Q4 Preview image-to-video](https://platform.vidu.com/docs/api-reference/video-models/vidu-q4-preview/image-to-video) and[Q4 Preview reference-to-video](https://platform.vidu.com/docs/api-reference/video-models/vidu-q4-preview/reference-to-video) API routes. The reference endpoint accepts one to fifteen images and output durations from three to sixteen seconds, with 540p, 720p, 1080p, 2K and 4K options. Audio output can be enabled or disabled; its default is true. These are documented API capabilities, not proof that the consumer app has identical controls or that Q4 produces better footage.


**A stored-subject workflow is not automatically portable to Q4 Preview.** The current reference endpoint explicitly does not support subject invocation yet. Supply permitted reference images through that endpoint’s supported inputs instead of assuming an existing subject ID is accepted. Test one representative shot before rebuilding a reusable-character workflow.


**Keep the start image and prompt controls explicit.** The[Q4 Preview image-to-video API](https://platform.vidu.com/docs/api-reference/video-models/vidu-q4-preview/image-to-video) accepts exactly one start image. Its` is_rec` setting defaults to true and uses an automatically recommended prompt to generate the video. For a comparison that holds your written instruction fixed, set` is_rec` to false and retain the returned prompt, model and settings with your results. These are API controls; confirm the consumer app’s actual inputs separately.


The verified USD pricing screen lists Q4 Preview at 19 credits per second for 720p and 78 for 4K. At the standard $0.005 rate, an eight-second request is a calculated $0.76 at 720p or $3.12 at 4K. It also displayed a limited launch pack of 30,000 credits for $105, or $0.0035 per credit, valid for twelve months. That is a dated prepaid offer, not a guaranteed permanent per-request checkout: buying the pack and using one clip still means spending $105, and unused credits expire under the displayed pack terms. Recheck the current package, currency and Console quote before paying.


**Retrieve completed Q4 API files before their links expire.** The endpoint documents creation and cover URLs as valid for twenty-four hours. Download the approved output into your own storage within that window. URL expiry is not evidence that Vidu deletes the underlying project at the same time, and it is not the consumer app’s retention policy.


## Reference-to-video vs image-to-video


[Vidu Reference to Video](https://www.vidu.com/ai-reference-to-video) is for reusable subjects and visual attributes across a prompted scene. Vidu says the web workflow accepts one to seven reference images and can derive character, object, style, composition, camera, scene, and effect references.


Use **reference-to-video** when the identity of a character or product must survive across several shots. Use **image-to-video** when you have one exact starting frame and mainly need to add motion. Use **start/end-to-video** when the opening and closing compositions matter. Use **text-to-video** when you are exploring ideas and have no required source visual.


These modes are not interchangeable. A single image can anchor a first frame while leaving later identity underconstrained. Multiple references provide more information, but conflicting angles, lighting, outfits, or product versions can confuse the model.


## How to prepare Vidu references


### 1. Define what cannot change


List the identity features that matter: face shape, hair, wardrobe, product silhouette, label placement, material, color, scene geometry, or art direction. If everything is “important,” the review becomes subjective.


### 2. Use clean, compatible references


Choose sharp images with a readable subject and minimal occlusion. For a character, include useful angles without switching wardrobe or age. For a product, keep the exact SKU, packaging, cap, label, and proportions consistent. Avoid mixing concept art, photography, and screenshots unless the style change is intentional.


### 3. Assign references explicitly


Name each subject in the prompt and say what the reference controls. Describe the action, setting, camera, timing, and elements that must remain fixed. Do not make the model infer whether one image defines a person, outfit, location, or color grade.


### 4. Test one short shot first


Run the shortest useful shot before spending credits on a full sequence. Confirm identity and composition, then change one variable at a time. A new prompt, reference set, model, duration, and resolution in the same retry cannot tell you what fixed or broke the result.


### 5. Review frames, motion, and audio separately


Pause on the first, middle, and final frames for identity and object drift. Watch at normal speed for motion and camera problems. Listen once without watching for speech, timing, noise, and music balance.


## A fair 15-minute Vidu test


Use one eight-second brief that resembles the work you plan to publish. Keep the same source assets, prompt, aspect ratio, duration, and resolution when comparing Vidu with another tool.


**Reference set:** one front three-quarter character or product image, one alternate angle, and one environment or style reference.


\[Subject from reference\] performs \[one action\] in \[setting\]. Preserve \[three identity details\]. Camera: \[one movement\]. Lighting: \[specific condition\]. End on \[clear final composition\]. Include \[dialogue or sound cue\] only if native audio is being evaluated.


[Try in Image-to-Video](https://magichour.ai/create/image-to-video?prompt=%255BSubject%2520from%2520reference%255D%2520performs%2520%255Bone%2520action%255D%2520in%2520%255Bsetting%255D.%2520Preserve%2520%255Bthree%2520identity%2520details%255D.%2520Camera%253A%2520%255Bone%2520movement%255D.%2520Lighting%253A%2520%255Bspecific%2520condition%255D.%2520End%2520on%2520%255Bclear%2520final%2520composition%255D.%2520Include%2520%255Bdialogue%2520or%2520sound%2520cue%255D%2520only%2520if%2520native%2520audio%2520is%2520being%2520evaluated.)


Generate three attempts in the same mode. Record the model, settings, queue time, credits charged, failures, and whether each clip passes:


1. The file plays and matches the requested aspect ratio and useful duration.
2. The subject or product remains identifiable from first to last frame.
3. Required text, logos, hands, faces, and object parts do not visibly break.
4. The requested action and camera move occur without a major unrequested scene change.
5. Dialogue, music, or effects are correct and synchronized when audio is required.
6. No visible defect requires regeneration before the intended use.


Compare cost per accepted clip, not the prettiest single frame.


## Best Vidu alternatives by job


### Magic Hour: broader browser workflow


[Magic Hour's AI Video Generator](https://magichour.ai/products/ai-video-generator) is the practical alternative when you want video generation alongside image creation, talking photos, face swap, lip sync, animation, and other media workflows in one account. Start here when the decision is broader than one Vidu model or when the next production step matters as much as the initial clip.


### Kling AI: model-specific cinematic generation


[Kling AI](https://kling.ai/) is relevant when you want to compare current Kling models, motion, camera behavior, native audio availability, and reference controls against Vidu. Match model version and settings; “Kling vs Vidu” is too broad if one side uses a fast model and the other uses a flagship route.


### Runway: generation plus editing


[Runway](https://runway.com/) is the better comparison when the workflow needs generation, transformation, timeline work, or production controls in one environment. Separate its web subscription from API billing and calculate the cost of the actual model and edit path.


### PixVerse: templates and fast social workflows


[PixVerse](https://pixverse.ai/) is relevant for effect-led clips, templates, mobile creation, and social formats. Compare its exact generation mode with Vidu reference-to-video rather than treating a template effect as the same product.


## Production and rights checklist


- Confirm the exact Vidu model, mode, duration, resolution, aspect ratio, and audio setting.
- Save the prompt, references, generation date, credits charged, and rejected attempts.
- Inspect identity, hands, logos, labels, product geometry, background continuity, and the final frame.
- Verify dialogue, speaker assignment, pronunciation, music, effects, and synchronization.
- Check the live plan for watermark, download, privacy, retention, commercial-use, and cancellation terms.
- Obtain permission for every likeness, voice, image, video, logo, product asset, and track.
- Do not present a generated scene as an authentic recording or customer testimonial.
- Keep a human editor responsible for factual claims, disclosures, and final publication.
